svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases, powered by AWS Glue Data Quality, which profiles and evaluates tables at catalog scale from a single configuration. You define data quality checks once for a catalog, a database, or a single table, and AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you choose. You can use built-in profiling options for common baseline statistics or provide your own Data Quality Definition Language ruleset with analyzers, rules, or both. Evaluations can run once at creation or on triggers, so they run on a schedule or whenever table metadata changes, including every Apache Iceberg commit. After three runs on a table, AWS Glue Data Quality flags anomalous statistics that drift outside expected bounds, which matches the documented requirement of a minimum of three data points to detect anomalies. The first thing to understand is the feedback loop: when an anomaly is detected it is considered normal for subsequent runs, and the machine learning algorithm will consider this anomalous value as input unless it is explicitly excluded, so retraining by acknowledging or rejecting anomalies is critical. At catalog scale, across thousands of tables, nobody performs that per-table triage, so a genuine regression is absorbed into the baseline within a few runs. Compounding this, when anomalies are generated data quality scores are not impacted, so an anomaly does not fail anything on its own. The second thing is mode selection: the Linear mode is the default and models trends and seasonality, and suits evaluations run on a regular schedule, while Fixed mode treats all data points as equally spaced and suits irregular or unpredictable intervals. The headline trigger of this launch, firing on every Iceberg commit, produces exactly the irregular intervals that Linear mode is documented as unsuited to, so the default mode is the wrong mode for the newly promoted trigger. The third thing is cost, and there is an asymmetry: there is no additional charge for detecting anomalies in AWS Glue ETL jobs, but in the Data Catalog you will incur 1 DPU per statistic for the time it takes to detect anomalies, on average between 10 to 20 seconds per statistic, at 0.44 dollars per DPU-hour billed per second with a one-minute minimum for evaluation tasks. At fifteen seconds per statistic that is roughly 0.0018 dollars per statistic, so ten thousand statistics across a thousand tables is about 18 dollars per full catalog pass, before the evaluation tasks themselves. There is no cost to store statistics, but there is a limit of 100,000 statistics per account and statistics are stored for a maximum of two years, so a catalog-wide configuration consumes a finite account-level budget. Finally, Glue gathers statistics only once even when both a rule and an analyzer cover the same columns, and the time component is crucial to the algorithm because limits differ for the same values over one-minute, hourly and daily intervals. The capability is available in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud US, and AWS China regions.
svg.title: Catalog-scale anomaly detection, and the anomaly it learns to call normal
svg.text: One configuration, every table — including the triage nobody will do.
“AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you
choose.”
The feedback loop that does not scale with the feature
“When an anomaly is detected, it is considered normal for subsequent runs. The machine learning
algorithm will consider this anomalous value as input unless it is explicitly excluded.”
Accuracy depends on a human acknowledging or rejecting each anomaly. Across a catalog of thousands of
tables, that triage does not happen — so a real regression becomes the new baseline in a few runs.
And an anomaly does not fail anything by itself
“When anomalies are generated, data quality scores are not impacted.”
So the signal needs a consumer you build. It will not block a pipeline on its own.
The default mode is wrong for the headline trigger
LINEAR (default) trends + seasonality · “you run evaluations on a regular schedule”
FIXED equally spaced · “irregular or unpredictable intervals”
A trigger on “every Apache Iceberg commit” is the irregular case. Set ObservationMode explicitly.
THE BILLING ASYMMETRY
In Glue ETL: “no additional charge for
detecting anomalies”.
In the Data Catalog — this launch —
“1 DPU per statistic”, 10–20 s each.
Same capability, two price models.
THE ACCOUNT-LEVEL CEILING
limit 100,000 statistics / account
kept max 2 years · storage free
1,000 tables x 10 statistics = 10,000 per
pass — about $18, and 10 passes to the cap.
The docs do not say if it counts series or points.
Three runs before anything is flagged: “a minimum of three data points to detect anomalies” — so a new table is unmonitored at first.
Interval matters to the model: “The limits will differ for the same values over a one-minute interval, an hourly
interval, or a daily interval” — so changing the cadence invalidates what the model has learned.
Available in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS China regions.
